planPurpose: Compare current authored FIX gates against retained LOW/MID/HIGH reversible profiles after the first human H2A playtest. Add stat-drift, event-frequency, housing, low-stat risk, and faction-chain telemetry. Do not freeze a profile automatically.

topEvents.label: Nothing particularly unusual happens this year. Several institutions remind you that this does not constitute a guarantee.
Another year passes while you remain mobile. This is no longer remarkable to you, which makes it increasingly remarkable to everyone else.
You attend another reunion and are once again the only person who arrives under her own power. Someone saves you the chair with the best view of everyone else.
A younger relative asks whether your committed material means you will stop aging soon. You discover that nobody in the family has a consistent answer.
A routine checkup confirms that you remain mobile despite increasingly unconvincing statistics. The doctor changes the subject to maintenance planning.
Everlasting Mutual updates another line of its actuarial guidance. The financial press spends a day debating whether the change is reassuring.
The Department issues another Material Status circular clarifying a rule that most people only learn exists when the clarification arrives.
Meridian launches another preservation service with a new name, a familiar maintenance contract, and a waiting list.
The Continuity Research Institute publishes another result that slightly changes how professionals describe a Permanent Form and not at all how ordinary people do.
The Order of the Last Posture appears in the news again over a ceremony, a property dispute, or both. The details differ more than the photographs.
Another future-form financing scandal is rumored to involve the Black Ledger. The organization, if it still exists, does not comment.
A family gathering lasts longer than planned. Nobody discusses preservation until dessert, which counts as progress.
An old friend asks how your material condition is progressing, then spends the rest of the evening talking about her divorce. You appreciate the change of subject.
You become one of the longest-mobile employees in your department. HR sends a congratulatory card and a preservation brochure in the same envelope.
You reorganize part of your life for reasons that feel important at the time. No institution manages to monetize this immediately.
You make a friend at school. You agree that neither of you wants to become part of the assembly hall.
You spend more time with classmates after school. Someone starts a rumor about everyone's future Permanent Form; yours is inaccurate but flattering.
You move homes and discover that the lease now asks for your projected floor-loading requirements. The agent calls this standard accessibility planning.
Exam season arrives again. Your school reminds students that stress-related mineral symptoms do not excuse late submissions.
Another school year ends with excellent marks. The school recommends an enrichment program and three additional forms.
You meet friends for dinner. Someone asks about your committed material, someone else changes the subject, and the evening improves immediately.
You take an advanced elective. The teacher warns that university credit is transferable but post-mobility credit is jurisdiction-dependent.
You attempt to get into better shape. Progress is slow, measurable, and not accepted by your insurer as a material-risk intervention.
Another year is mostly spent growing, falling down, asking questions, and being told not to touch things.
You change jobs for better pay. The new employer promises a 'modern approach to mobility continuity,' which means a newer PDF.

retentionPolicy.note: All omitted harnesses remain retained for H2B or future relevant regression work.

methodologyNotes: CURRENT_AUTHORED is the canonical corpus with no threshold rewrite at all. The Phase 1.1 `ORIGINAL_REFERENCE` profile is deliberately NOT used as the control: canonical gates changed after Phase 1.1, so that arm is historical rather than current.

LOW/MID/HIGH use the retained reversible rewrite in `src/sim/experiments.ts`, which rewrites assigned event FIX gates and the validity conditions of schedules pointing at them, in memory only. Canonical event JSON is never written.

Every arm uses the same base seed. A rewritten arm carries a derived content fingerprint, and the run seed is `contentVersion:seed`, so the arms are independent samples of the same sampling design rather than a paired comparison. This matches the retained Phase 1.1 experiment behaviour; at these run counts the sampling error on a rate near 50% is roughly ±0.9pp.
Species are stratified equally, so a species roll cannot drift between arms.
ARCHETYPE_SET priorities are read verbatim from the retained Phase 1.1 experiment matrix. No new archetype is invented and no allocation comparison is run.
Visible stats are unclamped in the canonical balance constants, and this run adds no clamp and changes no stat effect.
